findings.title: Materials' 50-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials sits at percentile 36 forward but 86 trailing, a 50-point gap that is the widest in the table. The forward multiple implies 108 percent earnings growth, which the market is pricing as if the current earnings collapse is temporary.

findings.title: Health Care's 99th percentile forward multiple is extreme
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E of 20.13 is at the 99th percentile of its five-year range, yet the trailing multiple is only at the 84th. Analysts are underwriting 84 percent earnings growth, a bet that looks stretched given the sector's already-rich valuation.

findings.title: Utilities' forward richness masks trailing cheapness
findings.body: Utilities trades at percentile 28 forward but percentile 8 trailing, a 20-point gap that has widened as the forward multiple rose 18 points in a month. The market is paying up for stability, but the implied 9 percent earnings growth hardly justifies the re-rating.
